title: It comes from a pool now — and here it is moving
question: Does this read as a waterfall now: a pool that spills over an edge, falls, and lands in another pool? And is the fall itself still too thin?
context_md:
You said it looked like it came from nowhere and went nowhere. Both halves are now built.

**Finding a source pool was impossible, so the pass cuts one.** And the measurement that killed the search is what made cutting work. Requiring the ground to *drop* behind a cliff lip matched nothing in 24 worlds — which means the opposite is true: the shelf behind a rim stands at or above the lip for a median 107–120 columns. That is exactly the back wall a pool needs. So `springs` now walks that shelf, cuts a tapered bowl into it, and fills it to the brim. The pool has two ways out — the cliff right there, and the far end of the shelf a hundred columns away — and it reaches the cliff first.

**The GIF** is a whole 512-wide world at 1:1, so it is one screen of play. **The still** is the same feature at the shipped size and 6x, where you can see the spray going over the lip: carved tarn on the right, spill in the middle, plunge pool at the foot on the left.

What I would still call unfinished: the fall is narrow, and I have not touched that. `render.rs` dims a liquid toward black by fill, so a thin sheet reads darker than it should. Tell me if it bothers you and I will go at it directly rather than guessing.

items.label: canyon, one screen, running
